opening: The record concerns a desert expedition decoding a chain of emergency beacons. By the time investigators reconstructed the transmission that redirected the rescue convoy, casual impressions had produced several plausible candidates. The reviewers therefore used only the local rules stated in the surviving record.

scenes.prose: Before comparing names, the panel read the governing notes aloud. For this incident, the board declared the coherent signal bearer protocol active; ordinary rank and reputation did not count. The panel fixed one shared status scale for the whole inquiry: clear counted as 0; dormant counted as 1; stable counted as 2; waking counted as 3; latent counted as 4; open counted as 5. The local tally began at 6. In order it used relation, temporal, causal, spatial, sequence, and protocol statuses with coefficients 11, 13, 5, 3, 2, 7. At each stream, the panel squared the current tally, added that stream's coefficient times its status value, and kept the remainder modulo 97. It made three passes: first in the stated order, then in reverse order with the coefficients reversed, then once more in the stated order with the coefficient list rotated one place left. Without resetting the tally, it repeated that complete three-pass cycle 115 times.
scenes.title: Reconstruction 1

scenes.prose: The inquiry moved from recollection to checked records. When the pairing sheet was recovered, Sawyer Okada's team pairing stood at stable. Even the damaged roster still marked Casey Rossi's team pairing as dormant. A clock-backed entry listed Morgan Okada's signal interval as stable. The repeater response that followed Drew Nguyen registered as clear. Causal review marked Gray Meier's repeater response open. Door and route checks placed Sawyer Okada's beacon sector at stable. Witnesses in the corridor put Casey Rossi's beacon sector at clear. Reconstruction kept Morgan Okada's relay order at latent. A close photograph of the token set Drew Nguyen's cipher glyph to latent. At final count, Gray Meier's cipher glyph remained stable.
scenes.title: Reconstruction 2

scenes.prose: The inquiry moved from recollection to checked records. A witness who checked the roster left Drew Nguyen with a waking team pairing. On the sealed worksheet, clerks wrote latent beside Gray Meier's team pairing. Clocked entries put Sawyer Okada's signal interval at dormant. The sequence sheet showed Casey Rossi's signal interval as waking. Downstream checks tied Morgan Okada to a latent repeater response. A movement sketch marked Drew Nguyen's beacon sector as latent. The route ledger tied Gray Meier's beacon sector to dormant. In the ordered log, Sawyer Okada's relay order appeared as waking. The ordered sheet showed Casey Rossi's relay order as clear. Inventory counted Morgan Okada's cipher glyph as dormant.
scenes.title: Reconstruction 3

scenes.prose: The inquiry moved from recollection to checked records. In the earlier pairing note, Morgan Okada carried a open team pairing. After the timesheet review, Drew Nguyen's signal interval stayed open. Reconciled timing notes kept Gray Meier's signal interval at latent. Instruments tracing Sawyer Okada's action left the repeater response dormant. When Casey Rossi acted, the repeater response came back waking. Location review left Morgan Okada's beacon sector waking. Sequence notes placed Drew Nguyen's relay order at dormant. At sequence review, Gray Meier's relay order stayed stable. Token and seal checks left Sawyer Okada's cipher glyph at clear. The sealed check showed Casey Rossi's cipher glyph as waking.
scenes.title: Reconstruction 4

scenes.prose: The inquiry moved from recollection to checked records. For this incident, the accepted tally was 58. The final definition was strict: the coherent signal bearer was the one person whose six-stream tally equaled the accepted tally.
